data.description:
## Context
Gerrit Verify currently runs thousands of repeated real Pandoc subprocess conversions over the complete DC wiki corpus. Run 31798375024 attributed at least 184.32 seconds of the macOS critical path to two visible corpus phases alone. The operator confirmed the architecture research and approved moving the complete real-Pandoc corpus replay to the External Integration Tests job. Current ADR 0095 explicitly requires every conversion assertion to use the real binary, so this testing-boundary change requires a narrow superseding ADR before implementation.

## Research decision
Popular maintained OSS precedent supports committed golden/static outputs plus compact live boundary probes: Pandoc uses literal writer outputs; nbconvert and pypandoc use small real-Pandoc probes; Kubernetes client-go commits golden request/response fixtures; Rust compiletest uses blessed output snapshots. The approved design keeps three representative live corpus bodies (code_arrow, table, prose) plus existing compact provenance probes in Gerrit Verify, moves complete real-Pandoc replay to the weekly/manual External Integration Tests workflow on Ubuntu and macOS, preserves every assertion class against committed outputs in Verify, and keeps deterministic regeneration plus version/binary-fingerprint drift failure. The 184.32-second figure is a lower-bound estimate; implementation must obtain paired A/B evidence.

## Plan
- Add a numbered ADR in docs/adr that narrowly supersedes ADR 0095 only where it mandates a real Pandoc process for every conversion assertion. Preserve the production segmenting renderer, pin/provenance, Linux/macOS platform boundary, fallback behavior, and every safety/fixed-point/richness assertion class.
- Amend ADR 0095 with a clear Superseded-by notice scoped to the testing-assurance clause.
- Update docs/architecture.md with the authoritative hot-path versus external-integration verification boundary.
- Regenerate the ADR index and number markers using scripts/gen_adr_index.py.
- Run ADR numbering/index guards, documentation/link checks, lint, and the repository commit-ticket verifier.
- Submit this documentation-only decision through Gerrit. Do not begin implementation until this ADR is merged after HOLD approval.

## Expected file impact
- docs/adr/0095-dc-segmenting-wiki-renderer.md
- docs/adr/0096-*.md
- docs/adr/README.md
- docs/adr/.numbers/0096
- docs/architecture.md

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The ADR cites the confirmed dependency and OSS research.
- [ ] The ADR preserves all production renderer invariants and narrows supersession to the test execution boundary.
- [ ] Gerrit Verify retains three representative live corpus contracts plus compact pin/provenance probes.
- [ ] Complete real-Pandoc corpus replay is assigned to the weekly/manual External Integration Tests workflow on Ubuntu and macOS.
- [ ] Every existing assertion class remains required against committed deterministic outputs in Gerrit Verify.
- [ ] Version and platform-binary fingerprint drift fail fast, and deterministic fixture regeneration remains documented.
- [ ] The ADR states that 184.32 seconds is a one-run lower bound and requires paired A/B implementation evidence.
- [ ] ADR 0095 and docs/architecture.md point to the superseding decision.
- [ ] ADR number/index and documentation guards pass.
- [ ] No implementation code or test-routing change is included in this ADR change.
- [ ] The ADR reaches HOLD in Gerrit; implementation begins only after explicit approval and merge.
data.title: ADR: move complete Pandoc corpus replay to external integration
